rationale: The workflow runs on every push and pull request to main with no concurrency control, so repeated revisions on the same branch/PR can run in parallel and waste resources. Pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (stale_run_cancellation) supports cancelling superseded runs partitioned by workflow and branch/PR, with reported estimated VM-time savings (free 1.9%, paid 4.1%). Its preconditions are met: runs represent the same workflow and branch/PR, a newer revision supersedes older checks, and there is no release/deployment work. Using group ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }} isolates distinct branches/PRs, addressing the contraindication that distinct branches must not share a cancellation group. All existing steps (checkout, yarn install with existing yarn cache, playwright install, lint, build, test, codecov) are preserved unchanged, so build/test coverage and required checks are kept intact. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is not applied because yarn dependency caching is already present via setup-node cache: yarn. A custom timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT) is not applied because there is no representative successful-duration history in ci_history and a fixed limit risks timing out valid slow playwright browser-install/test runs.
